text:
emily: Heads-up — I found a scoped role used by the backup uploader that also has kms:CreateGrant and kms:Decrypt on our DB CMK. Likely cause for reported restore-escapes yesterday. Trying to outline a quick remediation and want buy-in.

michael: Ugh. Can you paste the policy snippet? :eyes:

emily: Sure — minimal excerpt:
```
{
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:CreateGrant"],
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333:key/abcd-1234",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/backup-uploader"}
}
```
We inadvertently gave CreateGrant to the role so it can generate ephemeral grants for cross-account restore. That means a compromised uploader could mint grants to another principal.

sarah: Oh yeah that's a scoping smell. Attack path: assume uploader -> CreateGrant -> grant to attacker principal -> Decrypt backup data. We should remove CreateGrant from backup-uploader and instead use a short-lived, audited service account that runs grant issuance with strict conditions.

dmitri: Agreed. Also need to ensure CloudTrail logs KMS API calls and that CloudTrail is forwarding to secure logs with immutable retention. Was the CreateGrant call visible in logs for the incident?

emily: Not consistently — we saw a CreateGrant but only in the management account trail. Some accounts didn't have management trails enabled. Ops, can you confirm current trail coverage?

ops-bot: cloudtrail-check: management-trail=enabled in prod-master, account-children: acct-101=enabled, acct-102=disabled, acct-103=enabled. See https://redwood-internal/logs/trails

michael: So acct-102 is missing. That explains the partial visibility. Remediation plan item 1: enable org-level CloudTrail in all accounts, enforcement via SCP so nobody can disable it.

sarah: Remediation plan item 2: remove kms:CreateGrant from backup-uploader role. Replace workflow with a dedicated grant-service role that requires MFA and uses kms:ViaService or a specific condition on kms:GrantConstraints. Also add condition on kms:creategrant: "kms:GrantIsForAWSResource"? (depends on provider)

dmitri: We should also require a `aws:PrincipalTag` on any principal receiving grants (e.g., "role=redwood-grant-target"), and include `kms:GrantTokens` usage only via our orchestrator so human-initiated grants are denied.

emily: Draft IAM diff for backup-uploader (for approvals):
```
- Action: kms:CreateGrant
+ Action: kms:Encrypt,kms:GenerateDataKey
```
And a new policy for grant-service:
```
Action: ["kms:CreateGrant","kms:RevokeGrant"],
Condition: {
  "StringEquals": {"aws:PrincipalTag/role": "redwood-grant-target"},
  "Bool": {"aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent": "true"}
}
```

michael: Good. Also add CloudWatch metric filter for CreateGrant on the CMK and an alert to sec-oncall if CreateGrant occurs outside the grant-service principal. Quick correlate: `aws kms list-grants --key-id abcd-1234` + `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=CreateGrant`.

sarah: For incident response playbook, we should include: 1) Identify all active grants on CMK, 2) Revoke suspicious grants, 3) Rotate CMK if any unauthorized Decrypt observed, 4) Snapshot restore sandbox to validate data integrity, 5) Full IAM role audit for any role with kms:Decrypt/CreateGrant.

dmitri: Note on rotation: rotating a KMS symmetric key doesn't re-encrypt data; rekeying requires rewrap or create new key + re-encrypt. So if we rotate, we must plan restore windows. Might be heavy for large object-store backups. Consider revoking grants + rotating grant tokens first.

emily: Also propose short-term mitigation: add explicit deny for kms:CreateGrant on backup-uploader role via SCP on accounts where backup-uploader is used. That buys time.

ops-bot: policy-change-request submitted: SCP deny kms:CreateGrant targeting arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/backup-uploader in acct-101 and acct-103. ETA 30m.

michael: I'll own the CloudTrail org enablement ticket and the alert rule. sarah, can you own the grant-service policy + deploy pipeline? dmitri, lead the grant enumeration and revocation runbook.

sarah: On it. I'll post PR link when ready.

dmitri: Starting `aws kms list-grants` + `aws kms list-keys` sweep now, will post findings. If I find unexplained grants, I'll revoke with `aws kms revoke-grant --key-id abcd-1234 --grant-id <id>` and record in incident channel.

emily: Thanks all. Once PRs are merged we'll run a smoke test: create a restore flow without CreateGrant and ensure it still works for our supported cross-account use-case via the grant-service.

eng-bot: incident-note: ENG-SEC-2026-03-20-01 created. Linked to ticket: SEC-4072.

michael: Quick question — should we add an automated scanner to detect policies that include kms:CreateGrant across the org? I can add a cheap Lambda.

sarah: Yes please. Add it as part of the CI policy checks too — block PRs that add CreateGrant to non-whitelisted roles.

dmitri: One last thought: auditing snapshot metadata in the object store. Add a signed metadata field like `created_by_grant_service=true` so restores can assert provenance before decrypting.

emily: Love that. Add to TODOs.

michael: Ok, rolling on tickets. Will update here when trails are org-enabled and SCP applied. :thumbsup:
